mainTopic: Dividing a partnership without a בית דין; returning lost animals; honoring parents versus מצוות; unloading and loading a fallen animal
overview: The amud opens by finishing the story of רב ספרא, who divided a partnership's property on his own, without his partner and without a בית דין. רבה בר רב הונא says he needs proof that he divided before three. רב ספרא answers that taking your own share only reveals a fact, so two witnesses are enough, and he brings support from a widow who sells without a בית דין. אביי pushes back with רב נחמן's teaching that the widow still needs a בית דין of ordinary people. A new משנה then teaches when a lost animal must be returned, that a כהן may not become טמא to return it, and that a child must not obey a parent who says to break a מצוה. The same משנה also teaches the מצוות of unloading (פריקה) and loading (טעינה) a fallen animal. The גמרא defines the stable in the משנה, brings רבי יצחק's limit about the תחום in two versions, and finds the source for not obeying a parent. It ends by explaining that unloading is done for free and loading for pay, according to רבנן, while רבי שמעון says both are free, and each side argues from the פסוקים. רבא's new statement begins at the very end and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבה בר רב הונא's ruling: bring proof of dividing before three
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא tells רב ספרא he must bring two of the three who were present, or two witnesses who saw him divide before three.
steps.simpleTranslation: Bring two of the three people, or two witnesses who saw that you divided the property in front of a group of three.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes רבה בר רב הונא's instruction to רב ספרא, who divided a partnership's property on his own, without his partner and without a בית דין. He tells רב ספרא what kind of proof he needs to show he divided properly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה בר רב הונא holds that dividing a partnership must be done in front of three people, which counts as a בית דין. So רב ספרא needs proof that this happened, either from two of those three or from two other witnesses who saw it.

keyTerms.meaning: To divide (here: to split the partnership's property)
A group of three (a בית דין)

phrases.english: Two out of the three,
phrases.notes: Bring two of the three people who were there when you divided.

phrases.english: or alternatively, two witnesses
that you divided before a group of three.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dividing partnership property needs a group of three; proof is needed through two of them or two witnesses.

steps.title: רב ספרא asks for the source
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא asks רבה בר רב הונא how he knows that dividing must be done before a בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Where do you get this from?
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא asks for the source of the rule. This sets up the next step, where רבה בר רב הונא brings a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ספרא is not accepting the rule yet. He wants to know where it says that dividing property needs three people and not just two witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do you know this?

phrases.english: He said to him: From where do you have this?
phrases.notes: רב ספרא is the one asking here.

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that dividing property requires a בית דין.

steps.title: Proof from the משנה about the person returning a lost object
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא cites the משנה: someone who stops working to return a lost object sets his condition before a בית דין. If no בית דין is there, his own money comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: If there is a בית דין there, he makes his condition in front of them. If there is no בית דין, in front of whom can he make it? His own comes first.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר רב הונא answers with a משנה. It shows that making a binding claim on someone else's money needs a בית דין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the finder can only make his condition before a בית דין, and without one he cannot do it at all. רבה בר רב הונא learns from here that dealing with someone else's money in a binding way needs a בית דין, so the same should apply to splitting a partnership.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה

phrases.english: He said to him: As we learned:
If there is a court there –
phrases.notes: This is about someone who has to stop his paid work to return a lost object.

phrases.english: he makes a condition before them,
phrases.notes: His condition is that the owner will pay him for the work he lost.

phrases.english: if there is no court there –
before whom can he make a condition?
His own comes first.

steps.raayaObject: That dividing partnership property requires a בית דין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about the finder making his condition before a בית דין.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is the משנה of the finder's condition.

steps.title: רב ספרא: the cases are not alike
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא says the משנה is different: there, money moves from one person to another. Here he only took his own, so it is just revealing a fact, and two witnesses are enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it the same? There, he takes money from this one and gives it to that one, so we need a בית דין. But here, I took my own. It is just showing what happened, so two are enough.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא rejects the proof from the משנה. He explains why his case is different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the condition creates a new obligation on the owner's money, which needs a בית דין. When רב ספרא took his own share, nothing moved between people. The witnesses only need to show the fact that he divided fairly, and two witnesses are enough for that.

phrases.english: He said to him: Is it comparable?!
There, where he takes money out from this one
and puts it with that one, we need a court,
but here, I took my own,
phrases.notes: רב ספרא is talking about himself: he only took his own share.

phrases.english: it is merely revealing the matter,
two are enough for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between the finder's condition and dividing a partnership.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The finder moves money from one person to another. Taking your own share only reveals a fact.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets up a key difference: moving money between people versus simply showing what happened.

steps.title: רב ספרא's support: a widow sells without a בית דין
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא supports his view from the משנה that a widow may sell estate property for her support without a בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Know that this is true, as we learned: A widow sells without a בית דין.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא brings his own proof. A widow taking what she is owed from the estate does not need a בית דין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The widow is collecting what already belongs to her by right, like רב ספרא taking his own share. If she does not need a בית דין, neither does he.

keyTerms.meaning: Know that it is so (introduces a support)

phrases.english: Know that this is so, as we learned:

phrases.aramaic: אַלְמָנָה מוֹכֶרֶת שֶׁלֹּא בִּפְנֵי בֵּית דִּין!
phrases.english: A widow sells not before a court!
phrases.notes: She sells property from her husband's estate to pay for her support. See כתובות 97a.

steps.raayaObject: That taking what is yours does not need a בית דין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה that a widow sells without a בית דין.

steps.title: אביי: the widow still needs a בית דין of ordinary people
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges the widow proof. רב נחמן taught that the widow does not need expert judges, but she does need a בית דין of ordinary people.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But wasn't it said about that משנה, in the name of רב נחמן, that a widow does not need a בית דין of experts, but she does need a בית דין of ordinary people?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב ספרא's proof from the widow. The widow does need some kind of בית דין after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ספרא read the משנה as saying the widow needs no בית דין at all. רב נחמן explains it means no expert judges, but three ordinary people are still needed. So the widow case actually supports needing three, not just two witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it said about it?

steps.whatToRemember: Even the widow, who takes what is hers, needs three ordinary people. This challenges רב ספרא's claim that two witnesses are enough.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But wasn't it stated about it:
phrases.notes: "It" is the משנה about the widow.

phrases.aramaic: ״אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef bar Minyumi said that Rav Nachman said:

phrases.aramaic: אַלְמָנָה אֵינָהּ צְרִיכָה בֵּית דִּין שֶׁל מוּמְחִין,
phrases.english: A widow does not need a court of experts,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל צְרִיכָה בֵּית דִּין שֶׁל הֶדְיוֹטוֹת״?
phrases.english: but she does need a court of laymen?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וְלָאו מִי אִתְּמַר עֲלַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Undermines the widow proof from step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ספרא's proof that the widow sells without any בית דין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב נחמן says the widow still needs a בית דין of ordinary people. So taking what is yours still needs three, and two witnesses are not enough.

steps.title: Where the animal was found, and when not to listen to a father
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that an animal found in a stable does not need to be returned, but one found in a public area does. A כהן may not become טמא in a graveyard to return it. If a father tells his son to become טמא, or not to return the animal, the son must not listen.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone found an animal in a stable, he does not have to return it. If he found it in a public area, he must return it. If the animal was in a graveyard, a כהן may not make himself impure to get it. If his father told him 'Become impure' or 'Don't return it', he must not listen to him.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with the basic rules for returning a lost animal. It also sets limits on that obligation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal in a stable is in a safe place, so it does not count as lost. One in a public area is lost and must be returned. The duty to return it does not override a Torah prohibition, like a כהן becoming טמא. A father's command also cannot override any Torah law, whether it is to break a prohibition or to skip a מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; marks the start of the משנה text
A graveyard, which makes a כהן impure

steps.confusionAlert: The father case is not only about the graveyard. Even when the father says 'don't return it' about an ordinary lost animal, the son must still return it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a basic rule: honoring parents (כיבוד אב ואם) never permits breaking a Torah law.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
If he found it in a stable, he is not obligated to return it.
phrases.notes: 'It' means a lost animal.

phrases.english: In a public area, he is obligated to return it.
And if it was in a graveyard,
he may not become impure for it.
phrases.notes: This is talking about a כהן, who may not become impure from the dead.

phrases.english: If his father said to him, 'Become impure,'
or said to him, 'Do not return it,'
he should not listen to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ מְצָאָהּ בָּרֶפֶת – אֵין חַיָּיב בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה begins after the גמרא's discussion of the previous משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: You must return an animal found in a public place but not one found in a stable. Returning a lost object never permits breaking a Torah law, and a father's command cannot override a Torah law.

steps.title: Unloading and loading again and again
steps.stepSummary: If someone helped unload an animal and reload it, and it collapsed again, he must help again, even four or five times. The source is the doubled words 'עזב תעזב'.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he unloaded and loaded, then unloaded and loaded again, even four or five times, he is still obligated. The Torah says 'עזב תעזב', 'you shall surely release'.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a new מצוה: helping someone whose animal has collapsed under its load. It teaches that this duty can apply over and over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah repeats the verb 'עזב תעזב'. The משנה reads that repetition as meaning the duty applies again each time the animal collapses. Helping once does not end your obligation.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You shall surely release it', the Torah's doubled command

phrases.english: If he unloaded and loaded, unloaded and loaded,
even four or five times, he is obligated,
as it is stated: 'You shall surely release it.'
phrases.notes: שמות 23:5

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with a related מצוה of helping a fellow Jew's animal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The duty to unload and reload applies every time the animal collapses, even many times.

steps.title: When the owner just sits and watches
steps.stepSummary: If the owner sits down and tells the passerby to do the מצוה alone, the passerby is exempt, because the פסוק says 'עמו' (with him). But if the owner is old or sick, the passerby must help anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the owner went and sat down and said, 'Since the מצוה is on you, if you want to unload, unload,' the passerby is exempt. The Torah says 'with him'. If the owner was old or sick, the passerby is obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה limits the unloading מצוה. The passerby only has to help when the owner works together with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'עמו' teaches that this is a team job. An owner who refuses to help cannot dump the work on someone else. An owner who cannot help, because he is old or sick, still gets help.

keyTerms.meaning: 'With him', meaning together with the owner

steps.confusionAlert: The exemption is only for an owner who could help but chooses not to. An owner who is unable to help is a different case.

phrases.english: If the owner went and sat down, and said:
'Since the מצוה is on you,
if you want to unload, unload' —
he is exempt, as it is stated: 'with him.'
phrases.notes: Same פסוק, שמות 23:5: 'you shall surely release it with him.'

phrases.aramaic: אִם הָיָה זָקֵן אוֹ חוֹלֶה – חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: If the owner was old or sick, he is obligated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit to the unloading duty taught in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The passerby is exempt if the owner refuses to help, but obligated if the owner cannot help because he is old or sick.

steps.title: Is loading also a Torah מצוה?
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא says the Torah commands unloading but not loading. רבי שמעון says loading is also a Torah מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a Torah מצוה to unload, but not to load. רבי שמעון says: loading is also a Torah מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a מחלוקת about whether helping to load an animal is a Torah obligation like unloading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that unloading (פריקה) is a Torah מצוה. The disagreement is about loading (טעינה). At first glance the first opinion says loading is not a Torah מצוה, but the גמרא later explains that the argument is really about whether loading must be done for free (step 25).

keyTerms.meaning: From the Torah, a Torah-level law

steps.whatToRemember: This משנה teaches: return an animal that is truly lost; never break a Torah law to return it or because a parent said so; help unload again and again, together with the owner (unless he is old or sick); and the תנא קמא and רבי שמעון disagree about loading, which the גמרא explains as a dispute about whether it must be done for free (step 25).
steps.whyThisMatters: This מחלוקת about loading sets up the גמרא's coming discussion of the difference between פריקה and טעינה.

phrases.english: It is a מצוה from the Torah to unload,
but not to load.
phrases.notes: He means there is no Torah מצוה to load.

phrases.english: רבי שמעון says: also to load.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִצְוָה מִן הַתּוֹרָה לִפְרוֹק אֲבָל לֹא לִטְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה with a מחלוקת about whether loading is a Torah מצוה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: At first glance, the תנא קמא holds that only unloading is a Torah מצוה, and רבי שמעון holds that loading is one too. The גמרא explains (step 25) that the real dispute is whether loading must be done for free: the תנא קמא says loading may be for pay, and רבי שמעון says it is also free.

steps.title: No obligation when the animal is overloaded
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי rules that if the animal was carrying more than its normal load, a passerby is not obligated to help.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי הגלילי says: if the animal was carrying more than a proper load, you don't have to help, because the פסוק says 'under its burden', meaning a load the animal is able to carry.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes with one more limit on the unloading מצוה, taught by רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the words 'תחת משאו' (under its burden) as meaning a normal burden the animal can handle. If the animal was carrying more than that, the passerby is not required to help.

keyTerms.meaning: required to attend to it, obligated to deal with it
a load the animal can stand up under

steps.whatToRemember: The unloading מצוה applies only to a normal load. If the animal was overloaded, רבי יוסי הגלילי says there is no obligation.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:

phrases.aramaic: אִם הָיָה עָלָיו יָתֵר עַל מַשָּׂאוֹ –
phrases.english: If there was on it more than its proper burden,
one is not required to attend to it,
as it is stated: "Under its burden,"
phrases.notes: שמות 23:5

phrases.english: meaning a burden that it is able to stand under.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further limit to the unloading and loading laws in the previous steps of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the animal carries more than its proper load, the passerby is not obligated to help, based on 'תחת משאו'.

steps.title: רבא defines the stable in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the stable in the משנה is one that neither leads the animal to stray nor keeps it securely locked in.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא begins. רבא said: the stable the משנה talks about is one that doesn't cause the animal to wander off, but also doesn't keep it safely shut in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by going back to the first case of the משנה, an animal found in a stable. רבא defines exactly what kind of stable is meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three possible kinds of stable: one that leads the animal to stray, one that fully secures it, and one in between. רבא says the משנה is talking about the in-between kind. The next steps will prove this.

keyTerms.meaning: a stable or barn for animals
leads astray, causes to wander off
guards, keeps the animal safely in

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the animal isn't in a stable at all. He is saying it is a specific middle kind of stable: not dangerous, but not locked either.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rava said:
The stable that they mentioned
phrases.notes: He means the stable in our משנה.

phrases.english: is one that does not lead the animal to stray
and does not secure it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא by clarifying the stable case of the משנה summarized in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The stable in the משנה neither leads the animal to stray nor secures it.

steps.title: Proving both parts of רבא's definition from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows where each half of רבא's definition comes from in the wording of the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know it doesn't lead the animal astray? Because the משנה says the finder is not obligated. How do we know it doesn't secure the animal? Because the משנה even needed to say 'he is not obligated.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבא got each half of his definition from the wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the stable led animals to stray, the finder would have to step in, so the ruling 'not obligated' shows it is not a dangerous stable. The second proof comes from the fact that the משנה bothered to say this at all. The next step explains why that matters.

keyTerms.meaning: since it teaches, from the fact that it says
since it was necessary to teach
he is not obligated regarding it

phrases.english: That it does not lead to straying
is learned from the fact that it teaches: "He is not obligated in it."
And that it does not secure the animal
is learned from the fact that it was necessary to teach: "He is not obligated in it."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the textual source for each half of רבא's definition.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's two-part definition of the stable
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's ruling 'אינו חייב בה' and the fact that it needed to be stated

steps.title: Why the stable can't be a secure one
steps.stepSummary: If the stable were secure, the ruling would be obvious, since a finder outside would simply put the animal in such a stable. So the stable must not be secure.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you thought the stable was secure, think about it: when someone finds the animal outside, he returns it by putting it into such a stable. So if he finds it already inside, would the משנה need to tell us he doesn't have to do anything? Rather, the stable must not be secure. Yes, learn this from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second proof: why the fact that the משנה needed to teach this ruling shows the stable is not secure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting a lost animal into a secure stable already counts as returning it. So if the animal were already in a secure stable, it would be obvious that the finder has nothing to do. The משנה only needed to say this because the stable is not fully secure, so we might have thought he must act.

keyTerms.meaning: for if it enters your mind, if you were to think
learn from it, conclude from this

steps.whatToRemember: The stable in the משנה is a middle case: not dangerous (so no duty to act), but not secure either (so the משנה had to tell us there is no duty).

phrases.english: For if it enters your mind that it secures the animal,
now, if he finds it outside,
he brings it inside such a stable,
phrases.notes: Putting it into a secure stable already counts as returning it.

phrases.english: so if he finds it inside, is it necessary to teach this?
Rather, learn from it that it does not secure the animal.
Indeed, learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the second proof in step 13 and closes the discussion of רבא's definition.
steps.raayaObject: That the stable in the משנה does not secure the animal
steps.raayaSupportSource: A secure stable would make the משנה's ruling obvious and unnecessary
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The stable neither leads to straying nor secures the animal.

steps.title: רבי יצחק limits the stable case to inside the boundary
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's stable ruling, and רבי יצחק says it applies only when the animal is within the תחום.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if he found it in a stable, he is not obligated. רבי יצחק said: that is only when the animal is standing within the city boundary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the stable line of the משנה again and brings רבי יצחק's limit on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal in a stable near home is not really lost, so there is no duty. But רבי יצחק says this is only true within the תחום. If the stable is outside the boundary, the finder would be obligated.

keyTerms.meaning: the boundary area around a city

phrases.english: If he found it in a stable, he is not obligated.
Rabbi Yitzchak said:
And that is only where it is standing within the boundary.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְצָאָהּ בָּרֶפֶת אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב. אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the same משנה line about the stable and adds a location limit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal found in a stable is exempt from return only if it is within the תחום.

steps.title: Inference: a public area obligates even within the boundary
steps.stepSummary: From רבי יצחק's words, the גמרא concludes that an animal found in a public area must be returned even within the תחום.
steps.simpleTranslation: We can infer from this that in a public area, even within the boundary, he is also obligated to return it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from רבי יצחק's limit on the stable case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי יצחק needed the boundary condition only for the stable, the boundary does not help in a public area. An animal wandering in a public place counts as lost even close to the city, so the finder must return it.

keyTerms.meaning: by implication, from the general statement we can infer

steps.whatToRemember: Stable within the תחום: no obligation. Public area: obligation, even within the תחום.

phrases.english: By implication, in a public area
and even within the boundary,
he is also obligated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an implication from רבי יצחק's statement.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: An animal found in a public area must be returned even if it is within the תחום.

steps.title: Second version: רבי יצחק's condition goes on the public-area case
steps.stepSummary: Some teach רבי יצחק's condition on the later part of the משנה: one must return an animal found in a public area only when it is outside the תחום.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some people teach רבי יצחק's statement on the later part of the משנה, which says: if it was found in a public area, he must return it. רבי יצחק said: this is only when the animal is standing outside the תחום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of where רבי יצחק's statement belongs. Here it is attached to the public-area case, not the stable case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version (Steps 15-16), רבי יצחק's condition was on the stable ruling. Here it is on the public-area ruling: you must return an animal found in a public area only when it is outside the תחום. Moving the condition changes what we can learn from it, as the next step shows.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who teach it (a second version of a statement)
The later part of a משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix the two versions together. In the first version, רבי יצחק spoke about the stable. In this version, he speaks about the public area, so the result is different.

phrases.english: There are those who teach it on the later part:
phrases.notes: "It" means רבי יצחק's statement from Step 15, now placed on a different line of the משנה.

phrases.english: In a public area, he is obligated in it.
Rabbi Yitzchak said:
And that is when it is standing outside the city limits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of רבי יצחק's statement from Step 15, attaching it to the later part of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal found in a public area must be returned only if it is standing outside the תחום.

steps.title: Inference: a stable never requires returning
steps.stepSummary: From this version, the גמרא concludes that an animal in a stable need not be returned, even if it is outside the תחום.
steps.simpleTranslation: We can learn from this that in a stable, even if the animal is standing outside the city limits, he is still not obligated to return it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the second version of רבי יצחק's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק put his condition only on the public-area case, so the stable case keeps the משנה's plain ruling with no condition. That means a stable never requires returning, even outside the תחום. This is the opposite of the first version, where the stable case had the condition and the public area was always required.

keyTerms.meaning: By inference; from this we can learn

steps.whatToRemember: Version 1: stable means not obligated only within the תחום, and a public area is always obligated. Version 2: a public area is obligated only outside the תחום, and a stable is never obligated.

phrases.english: By inference, that in the stable,
even if it is standing outside the city limits,
he is also not obligated in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּלַל, דְּבָרֶפֶת אֲפִילּוּ עוֹמֶדֶת חוּץ לַתְּחוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion from the second version in Step 17, the same way Step 16 did for the first version.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to the second version, an animal found in a stable never has to be returned, even outside the תחום.

steps.title: Source for not obeying a parent who says to break a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a כהן in a graveyard, and a ברייתא asks how we know a son must not obey his father's command to become טמא or not to return a lost item.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: in a graveyard, he may not make himself טמא for it. The רבנן taught: from where do we know that if his father told him "become טמא," or told him "don't return it," he should not listen to him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic from the משנה, and a ברייתא asks for the source of a rule: a child may not obey a parent who tells him to break a מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה teaches that a כהן may not become טמא in a graveyard to return a lost animal. The ברייתא adds a related case: what if the father commands it, or commands him not to return a lost item? It asks for a source that he should not listen, which is answered in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: He may not make himself ritually impure

phrases.english: In a graveyard, he may not become impure for it.
phrases.notes: This is quoted from the משנה. It is talking about a כהן, who may not become impure from the dead.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
From where do we know that if his father told him, "Become impure,"
or told him, "Don't return it,"
that he should not listen to him?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מִנַּיִן שֶׁאִם אָמַר לוֹ אָבִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה, about the graveyard, and brings a ברייתא on it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that a child must not obey a parent's command to break a מצוה.

steps.title: The פסוק: everyone must honor God
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from the פסוק that joins fearing parents with keeping שבת: parent and child are both obligated in God's honor.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: "Every man shall fear his mother and his father, and you shall keep My שבתות; I am ה׳." This means you are all obligated in My honor.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its question with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק that commands fearing parents also commands keeping שבת and ends with "I am ה׳." That ending teaches that the parent, too, must honor God. So a parent cannot order a child to break God's מצוות, and the child must not obey.

keyTerms.meaning: You are all obligated in My honor

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic source that honoring parents does not include obeying them when they tell you to break a מצוה.

phrases.english: As it is said: "Every man shall fear his mother and his father,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:3

phrases.english: and you shall keep My Sabbaths; I am the Lord."
You are all obligated in My honor.
phrases.notes: "All" means the parent and the child alike.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״אִישׁ אִמּוֹ וְאָבִיו תִּירָאוּ וְאֶת שַׁבְּתוֹתַי תִּשְׁמֹרוּ אֲנִי ה׳״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of the ברייתא in Step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק joins fearing parents with keeping שבת and ends with "I am ה׳," so parent and child are both obligated in God's honor, and the child must not obey a command to break a מצוה.

steps.title: Why is a פסוק needed at all?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא implies that without the פסוק the son would obey. The גמרא asks why, since a simple עשה cannot push aside a לא תעשה together with an עשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason is that the Torah wrote "keep My שבתות." But if not for that, would I have said he must obey him? Why? This one, honoring parents, is only an עשה, and that one, a כהן not becoming טמא, is a לא תעשה and an עשה. An עשה cannot come and push aside a לא תעשה together with an עשה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that the ברייתא needed a פסוק, and challenges this: the rule should be obvious even without one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Honoring parents is just a positive command (עשה). A כהן becoming טמא breaks both a prohibition (לא תעשה) and a positive command (עשה). There is a known rule that an עשה can never override a לא תעשה joined with an עשה, so we should not need a special פסוק to tell the son not to obey.

keyTerms.meaning: But if it were not so

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether he should obey. Everyone agrees he shouldn't. The question is only why the ברייתא needed a פסוק to teach it.

phrases.english: The reason is that the Merciful One wrote
"You shall keep My Sabbaths"
but if it were not so,
I would have said he should obey him?
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Both mean obeying.

phrases.english: But why?
This is a positive command,
phrases.notes: Honoring parents, from שמות 20:12.

phrases.english: and that is a prohibition and a positive command,
phrases.notes: A כהן is forbidden to become impure from the dead (ויקרא 21:1), and he is also commanded to stay holy.

phrases.english: and a positive command does not come
and push aside a prohibition together with a positive command!

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דִּכְתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״אֶת שַׁבְּתוֹתַי תִּשְׁמֹרוּ״ הָא לָאו הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the פסוק brought in Step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's need for a פסוק to teach that the son must not obey his father's command to become טמא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A plain עשה (honoring parents) can never override a לא תעשה joined with an עשה (a כהן's tumah), so the rule should follow without a פסוק.

steps.title: The פסוק was needed because honoring parents is compared to honoring God
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that since honoring parents is compared to honoring God, we might have thought it is strong enough to override, so the פסוק teaches that he must not obey.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed. You might have thought: since honoring father and mother is compared to the honor of God, as it says here "Honor your father and your mother" and it says elsewhere "Honor ה׳ with your wealth," he should therefore obey him. So the פסוק teaches us that he should not listen to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by showing why we might have thought honoring parents is stronger than a normal עשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah uses the same word, "honor" (כבד), for parents and for God, which links the two. Because of that link, we might have treated honoring parents as stronger than a normal עשה, strong enough even to override a לא תעשה and an עשה. The פסוק "I am ה׳" teaches that even so, the son must not obey.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought to say

steps.whatToRemember: Even though honoring parents is compared to honoring God, a child must not obey a parent who tells him to break a מצוה, because the parent too must honor God.

phrases.english: It was needed.
It might enter your mind to say:
since honoring father and mother is compared
to the honor of the Omnipresent,
phrases.notes: "The Omnipresent" (מקום) is a name for God.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר כָּאן ״כַּבֵּד אֶת אָבִיךָ וְאֶת אִמֶּךָ״,
phrases.english: as it says here, "Honor your father and your mother,"
phrases.notes: שמות 20:12

phrases.english: and it says elsewhere, "Honor the Lord with your wealth,"
phrases.notes: משלי 3:9

phrases.english: therefore he should obey him;

phrases.aramaic: קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן דְּלָא לִשְׁמַע לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: it teaches us that he should not listen to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 21 by explaining why the פסוק was necessary.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: showing that the פסוק was needed to block a reasonable mistaken idea
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since honoring parents is compared to honoring God through the shared word כבד, it might be strong enough to override even a לא תעשה and an עשה, so the son should obey.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק "I am ה׳" teaches that parent and child are both obligated in God's honor, so the son must not obey.

steps.title: What does 'but not to load' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that unloading is a Torah מצוה but loading is not, and asks what that means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: It is a מצוה from the תורה to unload, but not to load. What does 'but not to load' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה and asking what it means. This sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה seems to say that only פריקה is a Torah obligation and טעינה is not. The גמרא wants to know exactly what 'not' means here, because the simple reading will cause a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: Unloading a burden off an animal
Loading a burden back onto an animal
From the Torah itself, a Torah-level obligation

phrases.english: There is a מצוה by Torah law to unload
but not to load.
What does 'but not to load' mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section on the משנה's rule about unloading and loading.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the משנה's phrase 'but not to load'.

steps.title: Loading also has its own verse
steps.stepSummary: If 'not to load' meant there is no מצוה at all, that is hard to accept, because the תורה writes a פסוק about loading too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means there is no מצוה to load at all, why is unloading different? It is written 'You shall surely release it with him.' About loading it is also written 'You shall surely lift it with him'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the simple reading, that there is no מצוה of loading at all, and knocks it down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unloading has a פסוק, but loading has its own פסוק as well. So it cannot be that טעינה is not a מצוה. The 'not' must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (trying out a reading that will be rejected)
You shall surely release it with him (the פסוק for unloading)
You shall surely lift it with him (the פסוק for loading)

phrases.english: If we say it means: but there is no מצוה to load at all,
what is different about unloading,
about which it is written: "You shall surely release it with him"?
phrases.notes: שמות 23:5

phrases.english: About loading too, isn't it written: "You shall surely lift it with him"!
phrases.notes: דברים 22:4

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests one possible answer to the question and rejects it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that there is no מצוה of loading at all.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תורה writes a separate פסוק for loading, so loading must also be a מצוה.

steps.title: Unloading is for free, loading may be for pay
steps.stepSummary: The 'not' means loading does not have to be done for free. You may ask to be paid. רבי שמעון says loading is also free.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: it is a מצוה from the תורה to unload for free, but not to load for free. Loading may be done for payment. רבי שמעון says: loading is also done for free.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct meaning of the משנה. Both are מצוות, and the difference is about payment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'not' in the משנה is about doing it for free, not about whether there is a מצוה. For פריקה you must help for free. For טעינה you must help but may charge. רבי שמעון disagrees and says both are free.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (giving the correct reading after rejecting one)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think loading is not a מצוה. It is a מצוה too; the only difference is that you may ask to be paid for it.

phrases.english: Rather: there is a מצוה by Torah law
to unload for free,
but not to load for free,
rather, for payment.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אַף לִטְעוֹן בְּחִנָּם.
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: also to load for free.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: מִצְוָה מִן הַתּוֹרָה לִפְרוֹק בְּחִנָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem by giving a new reading of the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Not to load' means there is no מצוה of loading at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Not to load' means not for free; loading may be done for payment, while רבי שמעון holds both are free.

steps.title: The משנה teaches the same as a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that, read this way, the משנה teaches exactly what a ברייתא says openly.
steps.simpleTranslation: We have learned in our משנה what the רבנן taught in a ברייתא: Unloading is for free, loading is for payment. רבי שמעון says: both this and that are for free.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that our משנה, as just explained, matches a ברייתא that says the same thing clearly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא states plainly what we had to work out from the משנה. This supports the new reading: the argument between רבנן and רבי שמעון is about payment for טעינה.

keyTerms.meaning: We have learned (it is already taught in our משנה)
The Rabbis taught (opening of a ברייתא)
This and that, both of them

phrases.english: We have learned here what the Rabbis taught:
Unloading is for free, loading is for payment.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: זוֹ וָזוֹ בְּחִנָּם.
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: both this and that are for free.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Links the explained משנה to a matching ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פריקה is free and טעינה is for payment; רבי שמעון holds both are free.

steps.title: Why רבנן say loading is paid
steps.stepSummary: רבנן reason that if loading were also free, the פסוק about unloading would be extra. So it must be teaching that only unloading is free.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבנן? If you think the law is like רבי שמעון, the תורה should have written only loading and not needed unloading. I would have said: loading, where there is no animal suffering and no money loss, is required. Unloading, where there is animal suffering and money loss, surely is required! So why did the תורה write unloading? To tell you: unloading is for free, loading is for payment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reasoning of רבנן and answers it. The answer shows that the פסוק about unloading must be teaching something extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר would teach פריקה from טעינה, because unloading involves צער בעלי חיים and חסרון כיס while loading does not. So the separate פסוק about פריקה would be extra, unless it teaches a difference. That difference is that פריקה must be free and טעינה may be paid.

keyTerms.meaning: If it enters your mind, if you think
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה
Is it not all the more so? (a קל וחומר)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic method: if a קל וחומר could teach something, the extra פסוק must be teaching a new law.

phrases.english: What is the reason of the Rabbis?
For if you think it is like Rabbi Shimon,
let the Merciful One write loading
and there would be no need to write unloading.
And I would say: Just as with loading,
where there is no suffering of animals
and no loss of money, one is obligated,

phrases.aramaic: פְּרִיקָה דְּאִית בָּהּ צַעַר בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים
phrases.english: then unloading, where there is suffering of animals
and loss of money, all the more so!
Rather, for what law did the Merciful One write it?

phrases.aramaic: לוֹמַר לָךְ: פְּרִיקָה בְּחִנָּם, טְעִינָה בְּשָׂכָר.
phrases.english: To tell you: unloading is for free, loading is for payment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the source for the רבנן side of the argument.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for רבנן's view that loading may be paid.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק of unloading is extra because of a קל וחומר, so it teaches that unloading is free and loading is paid.

steps.title: Why רבי שמעון needs both verses
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says both פסוקים are needed because we could not tell which פסוק is about loading and which is about unloading.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the reason of רבי שמעון? Because the פסוקים are not clearly defined.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי שמעון explains the extra פסוק of unloading, and gives his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון the פסוק of פריקה is not extra. The פסוקים do not make clear which act each one is about. Without both, we could not know that each act is a מצוה, so no payment difference can be learned.
steps.whatToRemember: Both פריקה and טעינה are מצוות. רבנן: unloading for free, loading for payment, learned from the extra פסוק. רבי שמעון: both for free, because both פסוקים are needed since it is not clear which is which.

phrases.english: And what is the reason of Rabbi Shimon?
Because the verses are not clearly defined.
phrases.notes: He means we can't tell which פסוק is about loading and which is about unloading, so both are needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי שמעון's answer to the רבנן's argument from the extra פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How רבי שמעון explains why the תורה wrote the פסוק of unloading.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוקים are not clearly marked as loading or unloading, so both are needed and neither is extra.

steps.title: Why do the רבנן reject רבי שמעון's claim?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבנן do not accept רבי שמעון's point that we cannot tell which פסוק is about loading and which is about unloading.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן: why don't they say, like רבי שמעון, that the פסוקים are not clearly marked?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the רבנן and asks how they would answer רבי שמעון's argument from the last step. This question sets up the next step, where the answer comes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 28, רבי שמעון said both פסוקים are needed because we can't tell which is about loading and which is about unloading. The רבנן's whole argument (step 27) depends on the פסוקים being clearly divided. So the גמרא now asks what makes them so sure.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis, why
[don't they say] the verses are not clearly marked?
phrases.notes: This is רבי שמעון's claim from the last step. The גמרא is asking why the רבנן don't accept it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how רבנן respond to רבי שמעון's claim in step 28
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבנן think each פסוק clearly refers to one specific case

steps.title: Each פסוק points to its own case
steps.stepSummary: רבנן answer: one פסוק says the animal is lying under its load, which means unloading. The other says the animals are fallen on the road, which means the animal and its load are both on the ground, so it needs loading.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it is written 'lying under its burden.' There it is written 'fallen on the way,' which means the animals and their loads are lying on the road.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the רבנן's answer: the wording of each פסוק shows which case it is about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Lying under its burden' means the load is still on the animal, so it needs to be taken off: unloading. 'Fallen on the way' sounds like the animal and its load are both down on the road, so it needs to be loaded back up. Since the cases are clear, the רבנן's reading from step 27 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Lying under its burden (the unloading פסוק)

steps.title: רבי שמעון: 'fallen on the way' can also mean unloading
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון answers that 'fallen on the way' could mean the animals fell with their loads still on them. So that פסוק might also be about unloading, and the פסוקים are not clearly divided.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון: 'fallen on the way' can mean they fell with their loads still on top of them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון explains why he still says we can't tell the פסוקים apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן read 'fallen on the way' as the load lying on the road beside the animal. רבי שמעון says it can also mean the animal fell while the load stayed on its back, which is an unloading case. Since this פסוק is unclear, we need both פסוקים, and neither one is extra.
steps.whatToRemember: רבנן: each פסוק clearly fits one case, so the extra unloading פסוק teaches that only unloading is free. רבי שמעון: 'fallen on the way' is unclear, so both פסוקים are needed, and loading is also free.
